payload.vision: Vigil is the trust layer for autonomous coding agents: a cockpit that makes an agent run observable while it happens and provable after it ends. It never accepts a claim it has not independently verified — every PASS is backed by bytes on disk, every destructive action passes a rail, and every report is rendered from Vigil's own recorded observations rather than the agent's prose. The road to v1.0 turns that promise from something that works on one engineer's laptop into something any operator can install, trust and prove: the finished work reaches main instead of rotting on branches, the evidence check inspects content rather than byte counts, no report asserts a check the code never performed, no gate can silently go unenforced, the budget guard actually stops the run, and the artifacts are safe to hand to an auditor.

targetAudience.primary: The author/operator — a solo engineer running high-risk, multi-phase deployment and migration work through a Claude Code agent, who needs hard proof that each step actually happened rather than agent prose claiming it did.
secondary: AI-assisted engineering leads auditing what an autonomous coding agent did on a production-adjacent machine
Platform/DevOps engineers running gated validation plans in CI or over SSH via --plain and --json modes
Teams adopting the Claude Agent SDK who need observability, safety rails and cost visibility around agent runs
Reviewers/auditors who read run artifacts (events.jsonl, gates.json, cost.json, summary.json) after the fact without the TUI

features.title: Neutral default rails with environment profiles
features.description: Replace DEFAULT_RAILS' author-specific content with a portable, generic deny/warn set (destructive git operations, pattern kills, home-directory deletion, agent-instruction file edits) that contains no absolute user paths, hostnames or ports. Move the OmniRoute-specific rails (warn-real-omp-config, warn-live-db, no-checkout-main's Desktop/OmniRoute path) into a shipped example profile under profiles/, loadable via config. Introduce path-token interpolation (${HOME}, ${planRoot}, ${cwd}) so rails can express machine-relative intent portably.
features.rationale: This is the single hardest adoption blocker. Five of seven default rails reference the author's machine; one silently fails to protect anyone else's repo because it hardcodes a Desktop/OmniRoute path. Without this, every other feature is invisible to every other user.
acceptanceCriteria: A grep for '/Users/nick', 'OmniRoute', '.omp', '20128', '20219', '20239' and 'launchctl' across src/ and shipped config returns zero matches

DEFAULT_RAILS protects against git stash, git checkout/switch outside a worktree, pkill -f/killall, rm -rf on any home directory, and edits to CLAUDE/AGENTS/GEMINI.md using patterns that contain no absolute user paths
Rail match strings support ${HOME}, ${planRoot} and ${cwd} interpolation, resolved at config load and unit-tested for each token
profiles/omniroute.json reproduces the previous author-specific rail behaviour and is loadable via config.profile or --profile
Existing tests in verdict-rails.test.ts pass unmodified against the neutral rail set, with added cases proving the checkout rail now fires for an arbitrary repo path
Loading an unknown profile name fails config validation with a named error listing available profiles

userStories.as_a: engineer installing Vigil for the first time
userStories.i_want: default safety rails that protect my repository rather than someone else's
userStories.so_that: I get real blast-radius protection without reading and rewriting the rail source

userStories.as_a: operator with a specific production environment
userStories.i_want: to layer an environment profile of extra rails on top of the neutral defaults
userStories.so_that: I can encode my own live databases and config files as warn/deny targets without forking the tool

features.title: `vigil init` config and plan scaffolding
features.description: An interactive and --yes-scriptable init command that detects the environment (Claude Code binary location, git root, whether a worktree is in use), writes a validated vigil.config.json with sensible neutral defaults, optionally scaffolds a phases/ skeleton with an example PLAN.md and ROADMAP.md, and prints the resolved configuration including which rails are active and where runs will be written.
features.rationale: Discovery shows install is `npm link` from a Desktop checkout with no documented path from zero to a first run. Pairing a neutral rail set with a scaffold turns a two-hour archaeology session into a single command.
acceptanceCriteria: `vigil init` in an empty directory writes a vigil.config.json that passes ConfigSchema.parse without edits
`vigil init --yes` runs non-interactively with zero prompts and is safe to invoke in a script
Init resolves and reports the Claude Code executable using the existing --claude-bin → CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH → which claude → SDK default chain, and warns clearly if none is found
`vigil init --with-plans` scaffolds phases/01-example/01-01-PLAN.md plus ROADMAP.md that parse cleanly through the existing plan parser and produce at least one validation gate
Init refuses to overwrite an existing vigil.config.json unless --force is passed
Post-init output lists active rail ids, the resolved runs/ directory, the model, and whether settingSources is empty (clean agent)

userStories.i_want: one command that produces a working configuration
userStories.so_that: I can run my first gated plan without reverse-engineering the Zod schema

userStories.i_want: a scaffolded example plan that already satisfies the runner contract
userStories.so_that: I learn the Capture and verdict-line format by example rather than by failed runs

features.title: Content-aware evidence assertions with hash recording
features.description: Extend Capture targets from existence-plus-non-zero-bytes to declarative content assertions: minimum byte size, regex match, JSON-path existence or value comparison, and expected line count. Record a SHA-256 hash and byte size of every verified artifact into gates.json. A PASS whose assertion fails is downgraded to FAIL with the specific failing assertion injected back into the live session, reusing the existing evidence-downgrade path.
features.rationale: The product's core differentiator is that verdicts are evidence-checked rather than trusted, but the check is currently satisfied by any non-empty file. An agent that writes one byte of garbage to the Capture path passes the gate — the exact failure mode Vigil exists to prevent. Hashes also unlock run comparison in Phase 4.
acceptanceCriteria: The plan parser accepts assertion syntax on Capture lines covering at minimum: minBytes, matches (regex), jsonPath, and equals/contains for the resolved value
A Capture target with no assertion retains today's existence + non-zero-bytes semantics, so all existing fixture plans pass unchanged
A gate claiming PASS whose artifact exists but fails its regex assertion is recorded as FAIL in gates.json with a reason naming the assertion and the artifact path
The failing-assertion instruction is injected into the live session via the existing inject path and appears in events.jsonl
GateRecord.evidence entries gain sha256 and bytes fields, populated for every verified artifact including glob/brace expansions
Assertion evaluation is bounded: files above a configurable maxAssertBytes are streamed or rejected rather than read wholly into memory
Unit tests cover each assertion type passing and failing, plus malformed assertion syntax producing a parse-time error rather than a silent skip

userStories.as_a: operator running a deployment validation plan
userStories.i_want: gates to verify that evidence files contain what they should, not merely that they exist
userStories.so_that: an agent cannot satisfy a gate by touching an empty or garbage file

userStories.as_a: auditor reading gates.json after the fact
userStories.i_want: a cryptographic hash of every artifact that backed a PASS
userStories.so_that: I can prove the evidence on disk today is the evidence the gate actually accepted

features.title: Enforced budget and turn guards
features.description: Implement Vigil-side enforcement of maxBudgetUsd and maxTurns: track cumulative cost across plans in a run, emit a budget.warn RunEvent at configurable thresholds (default 75% and 90%), and hard-stop the run at 100% by interrupting the turn, writing a terminal budget.exceeded event and exiting non-zero. Surface remaining budget as a live header element in the cockpit and in --plain output.
features.rationale: maxBudgetUsd is accepted in config and handed to the SDK but never enforced locally, and cost is reported by the SDK rather than independently guarded. For a tool whose premise is walking away from an autonomous run, an unenforced spend cap is a direct financial risk.
acceptanceCriteria: Cumulative run cost is accumulated from session.result events across all plans and persisted to cost.json as a run-level total
Crossing a warn threshold emits a budget.warn RunEvent exactly once per threshold and renders visibly in both the TUI header and --plain output
Reaching maxBudgetUsd interrupts the active turn, halts plan sequencing, writes a budget.exceeded event and exits with a distinct non-zero code
maxTurns is enforced with the same warn-then-stop semantics
When no maxBudgetUsd is configured, behaviour is unchanged and no budget events are emitted
A unit test drives synthetic session.result events past the cap and asserts the run halts before the next plan starts
The cockpit header shows spend against cap as an absolute and percentage value when a cap is set

userStories.as_a: operator starting a long autonomous run and walking away
userStories.i_want: a spend cap that actually stops the run
userStories.so_that: a runaway loop cannot cost me hundreds of dollars overnight

userStories.i_want: to see remaining budget live
userStories.so_that: I can intervene before a cap forces an abrupt halt mid-phase

features.title: Secret redaction in run artifacts
features.description: Redact secrets before they reach disk. Apply a configurable redaction pass to tool inputs/outputs and event payloads covering known token shapes (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and the configured authTokenEnv value, sk- prefixed keys, bearer headers, AWS keys, private key blocks, .env assignments) plus user-supplied redact patterns. Replace matches with a stable placeholder that preserves a hash prefix so distinct secrets remain distinguishable in an audit without being recoverable.
features.rationale: Tool artifacts store full inputs and outputs verbatim, and runs/ is never pruned. Every run that reads a .env or echoes a header writes a live credential to disk permanently — an audit trail that is itself a liability, which blocks sharing run artifacts with the auditors the product targets.
acceptanceCriteria: Redaction is applied in RunStore.append before any write, so events.jsonl, tools/*.txt, gates.json and cost.json are all covered by a single chokepoint
The resolved auth token value is redacted by exact match regardless of pattern coverage
Built-in patterns detect sk-* keys, Authorization/Bearer headers, AWS access key ids and secrets, PEM private key blocks, and KEY=value assignments for names matching /TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|KEY/
config.redact accepts additional user regex patterns, validated at config load with a clear error on an invalid pattern
Redacted values render as [redacted:<8-char-hash>] so two different secrets remain distinguishable across a run
Redaction throughput is benchmarked and adds under 10% overhead on a synthetic 10k-event run
A test writes a fixture tool output containing each supported secret shape and asserts no raw secret survives to disk

userStories.as_a: operator whose agent reads .env files during a run
userStories.i_want: credentials scrubbed from run artifacts automatically
userStories.so_that: my audit trail is not a permanent plaintext secret store

userStories.as_a: engineering lead reviewing an agent run
userStories.i_want: to share a runs/ directory with a colleague or auditor
userStories.so_that: the evidence can be reviewed without leaking production credentials

features.title: Schema-validated SDK message boundary
features.description: Replace every `as unknown as {...}` cast in the session handlers with Zod schemas that parse incoming Claude Agent SDK messages (assistant/partial/result/rate_limit/tool_use/tool_result) at the boundary. Unknown or malformed shapes are surfaced as a typed `diagnostic` RunEvent naming the offending message type and failing path, and written to disk, rather than throwing deep inside a handler or silently yielding undefined. Parsing is permissive on unknown extra fields and strict on the fields Vigil actually reads.
features.rationale: The tool's entire observability claim rests on correctly reading SDK messages, yet every read goes through an unchecked cast against an exactly-pinned SDK version. A schema change today produces undefined tokens, missing verdicts and silently wrong cost accounting mid-run on a production-adjacent machine. This is the highest-severity technical risk in the repository and it blocks upgrading the SDK at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Zero `as unknown as` casts remain in src/engine/session.ts, enforced by a test that greps the source
Every SDK message consumed by Vigil has a named Zod schema whose parse-failure path is unit-tested with a malformed fixture
A malformed message produces a `diagnostic` RunEvent containing the message type and the failing field path, is appended to events.jsonl, and does not abort the run
Unknown additional fields on an SDK message are tolerated without a diagnostic; missing required fields always produce one
Cost, token and rate-limit values are read only through validated schemas; a missing total_cost_usd yields an explicit unknown rather than NaN or 0
A recorded real-session message corpus parses with zero diagnostics

userStories.as_a: operator running a long autonomous session
userStories.i_want: malformed agent messages to surface as visible diagnostics instead of silent undefined values
userStories.so_that: I can trust that a quiet cockpit means nothing went wrong rather than that parsing failed

userStories.i_want: a validated boundary that tells me exactly which message shape changed
userStories.so_that: I can upgrade without auditing every cast by hand

features.title: Continuous integration pipeline with coverage reporting
features.description: Add a GitHub Actions workflow running typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`), the full vitest suite and the build on every push and pull request against Node 20 and 22. Publish coverage via vitest's v8 provider with a floor that fails the job on regression, and surface a status badge in the README. Keep the workflow dependency-light and under two minutes so it never becomes a reason to skip it.
features.rationale: There are 27 tests covering the risky pure logic and no automation that runs them. With a bus factor of one, two commits of history and no issue tracker, CI is the cheapest possible substitute for a second reviewer, and it is a prerequisite for safely widening the SDK version range or accepting any outside contribution.
acceptanceCriteria: Push and pull_request events trigger typecheck, test and build jobs on Node 20 and Node 22
A deliberately introduced type error or failing test fails the workflow
Coverage is collected and reported as a job summary, with a configured minimum that fails the job when line coverage drops below the committed floor
The full workflow completes in under two minutes on a cold cache
README displays a CI status badge reflecting the default branch

userStories.i_want: every push to be typechecked, tested and built automatically
userStories.so_that: I find regressions before a run on a production-adjacent machine finds them

userStories.i_want: a visible green pipeline and coverage figure
userStories.so_that: I can trust the project is maintained and see whether my change broke anything

features.title: SDK contract fixtures and widened version range
features.description: Capture a corpus of real Claude Agent SDK message streams as committed JSONL fixtures and add contract tests that replay them through PlanSession against a stubbed SDK, asserting the resulting RunEvent sequence, gate verdicts and cost totals. With that safety net in place, relax the exact version pin to a caret range and add a CI job that runs the contract suite against the newest satisfying SDK release.
features.rationale: The SDK version is pinned exactly because nobody can tell whether an upgrade breaks anything — which means the project is permanently frozen on 0.3.261 and will accumulate an unpayable upgrade debt. Recorded fixtures turn 'we cannot upgrade' into a two-minute check, and they are the only way to get end-to-end coverage of the runner without burning tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: A committed fixture corpus covers at least a passing gate, a failing gate, an evidence-downgraded PASS, a rail deny, a tool approval and a rate-limit event
Replaying each fixture through a stubbed SDK produces a deterministic RunEvent sequence asserted in full
An end-to-end test runs a multi-plan fixture plan set through Runner against the stub and asserts final verdicts, generated reports and on-disk artifacts
The @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk dependency uses a caret range rather than an exact pin
A scheduled or matrix CI job installs the newest satisfying SDK version and runs the contract suite, failing loudly on a shape change
Contract tests execute without network access or API credentials

userStories.i_want: contract tests over recorded SDK streams
userStories.so_that: I can upgrade the SDK confidently instead of freezing on a pinned version forever

userStories.i_want: an end-to-end test against a stubbed SDK
userStories.so_that: I can verify my change without spending tokens or touching a real agent

features.title: Rail evaluation over resolved command semantics
features.description: Upgrade rails from regex matching on a flattened `<tool> <primary> <json input>` string to evaluation over a parsed shell command: tokenize the command, expand simple variable assignments, resolve quoting, and evaluate rails against each resolved argv plus the normalized absolute paths it touches. Flag known obfuscation vectors (base64 pipes into a shell, `eval`, `sh -c` with a constructed string) as a deny-by-default `unanalyzable` category, and keep the raw-regex path available for user rails that want it.
features.rationale: Rails are the only thing standing between the agent and the filesystem in the default `auto` mode, which runs with bypassPermissions. Today they can be defeated by `X=stash; git $X` or a base64 pipe, and they simultaneously produce false positives on innocent strings that merely mention a pattern. A safety control that is trivially bypassable is worse than none because it creates false confidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Bash commands are tokenized and simple variable indirection is resolved before rail evaluation; `X=stash; git $X` is denied by the git-stash rail
Paths in resolved arguments are normalized to absolute form before path rails are evaluated, so `../../` traversal and `~` expansion are matched
Commands containing eval, base64-to-shell pipes or `sh -c` with a non-literal argument are classified unanalyzable and denied by default, with the classification configurable
A documented false-positive corpus (commands merely mentioning rail keywords in strings, comments or filenames) produces zero denies
A documented bypass corpus of at least ten obfuscation attempts is denied, each covered by a test
Deny-wins-over-warn precedence and existing rail configuration syntax remain backward compatible

userStories.as_a: operator running in auto approval mode
userStories.i_want: rails that evaluate what a command will actually do rather than how it is spelled
userStories.so_that: an agent cannot defeat my blast-radius protection with a shell variable

userStories.i_want: matching against resolved arguments and absolute paths
userStories.so_that: my rails stop firing on harmless commands that merely mention a keyword

features.title: Rail lint and dry-run command
features.description: Add `vigil rails check` to validate the active rail set (compile every pattern, report unreachable or duplicate rails, flag patterns containing absolute user paths) and `vigil rails test '<command>'` to show which rails a candidate command would hit and the resulting verdict, without starting a session. Include an `--explain` mode that prints the resolved argv and normalized paths the rail engine actually evaluated.
features.rationale: Rails are safety-critical configuration authored by hand as regular expressions, and today the only way to discover that a rail is wrong is to have it fail to fire during a live destructive command. A dry-run makes safety configuration verifiable before the blast radius is real, and it is what makes VG-009's semantic engine legible.
acceptanceCriteria: `vigil rails check` exits non-zero and names each offending rail when a pattern fails to compile, duplicates another, or embeds an absolute home-directory path
`vigil rails test '<command>'` prints every matching rail, its action, and the final deny/warn/allow verdict
`--explain` prints the resolved argv and normalized absolute paths the engine evaluated for the command
Both subcommands work without a plan root, a Claude binary or network access
Output is available as JSON via `--json` for scripted verification of a rail set

userStories.i_want: to test a dangerous command against my rails before any agent runs
userStories.so_that: I learn my rails are wrong from a dry run rather than from a deleted branch

userStories.as_a: platform engineer managing shared rail profiles
userStories.i_want: a lint command I can run in CI over our rail config
userStories.so_that: a broken rail set cannot be merged

features.title: Artifact, config and probe test coverage
features.description: Close the named testing gaps outside the pure logic: RunStore artifact tests (events.jsonl append ordering and JSON validity, tools/NNNN naming and collision behaviour, gates.json and cost.json shape, session.json round-trip), config tests (file discovery precedence, CLI override merging, unsetEnv and env building, base URL and token routing), and probe tests (HTTP and shell probes with regex expectation, timeout and failure paths) against a local stub server.
features.rationale: The disk artifacts are the product's source of truth and its audit evidence, yet nothing tests that they are written correctly; config and env building decide whether a run is reproducible and whether a token reaches the right endpoint. These are exactly the untested layers where a silent defect destroys the audit trail rather than announcing itself.
acceptanceCriteria: Every line written to events.jsonl is asserted to be valid standalone JSON parsing back to the originating RunEvent, in order, for a synthetic run of at least 200 events
Tool artifact filenames are asserted for zero-padded ordering and collision-free naming across concurrent tool calls
gates.json, cost.json and session.json are asserted against their documented shapes, including the per-model and cache-token cost split
Config precedence is tested across CLI override, ./vigil.config.json and ~/.config/vigil/config.json, including the settingSources default of []
Child env building is tested for unsetEnv removal, env overrides, and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/AUTH_TOKEN routing, asserting no token leaks into an unrelated variable
HTTP and shell probes are tested against a local stub for success, regex-expectation mismatch, non-zero exit and timeout, each emitting the expected probe RunEvent

userStories.i_want: guaranteed well-formed and complete on-disk artifacts
userStories.so_that: my post-hoc analysis is not defeated by a truncated or malformed log line

userStories.i_want: coverage of config and env building
userStories.so_that: a refactor cannot silently reintroduce leaked local Claude Code settings

features.title: Non-blocking buffered event writer
features.description: Replace the per-event `appendFileSync` on the hot path with a buffered, backpressure-aware async writer that batches RunEvents and tool artifacts, flushes on an interval and on size, and always flushes synchronously on process exit, SIGINT and crash. Preserve the disk-first guarantee by acknowledging an event to the UI only once it is durably queued, and emit a diagnostic if the queue ever grows beyond a configured bound.
features.rationale: Synchronous filesystem calls on every event throttle chatty runs, which is precisely when observability matters most, and the TUI renders on the same thread. Buffering makes long autonomous runs smooth without weakening the disk-first principle that the event log — not the cockpit — is the source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: A synthetic 10,000-event run completes with no dropped or reordered events and measurably lower wall-clock time than the synchronous implementation, asserted by a benchmark test
SIGINT, uncaught exception and normal exit each flush all buffered events and tool artifacts before the process terminates, verified by a subprocess test
Event ordering in events.jsonl matches emission order exactly under concurrent tool-artifact writes
Queue depth beyond a configured bound emits a diagnostic RunEvent and applies backpressure rather than growing unbounded
`vigil tail` continues to follow a live run with no more than one flush interval of added latency

userStories.as_a: operator running a chatty multi-hour plan
userStories.i_want: a cockpit that stays responsive under heavy tool output
userStories.so_that: the observability layer does not become the bottleneck

userStories.i_want: a guarantee that an interrupted run still flushed its events
userStories.so_that: I can audit runs that were killed mid-flight

features.title: Versioned structured output and machine-readable exit summary
features.description: Add `--json` to `run` and `prompt`, emitting newline-delimited JSON of the same RunEvent stream to stdout, plus a final versioned summary object (schema_version, run id, per-plan verdicts, gate table with evidence hashes, cost, rate-limit utilization, rail hits, exit reason). Write the identical summary to runs/<id>/summary.json, and document the schema as a committed JSON Schema so consumers can validate it.
features.rationale: The CI and SSH audience is explicitly a target, but --plain emits human prose that a pipeline has to scrape. A stable versioned contract is what turns Vigil from a tool an operator watches into a step a pipeline can gate on, and summary.json makes the auditor persona work without the TUI or a JSONL parser.
acceptanceCriteria: `vigil run --json` writes only newline-delimited JSON to stdout; all human-readable logging goes to stderr
The final summary object includes schema_version, run id, per-plan verdicts, a gate table with evidence paths and hashes, total and per-model cost, rail hits and a typed exit reason
runs/<id>/summary.json contains a byte-identical summary object and is written even when the run fails or is interrupted
A committed JSON Schema validates the summary, and a test asserts emitted summaries validate against it
Exit codes are documented and distinct for success, gate failure, budget halt, rail-blocked halt and internal error
--json implies non-interactive operation and is compatible with --plain

userStories.as_a: platform engineer running Vigil in CI
userStories.i_want: a stable versioned JSON summary of the run
userStories.so_that: my pipeline can gate on gate results without scraping prose

userStories.i_want: a single summary.json per run
userStories.so_that: I can review what happened without replaying the TUI or parsing events.jsonl

features.title: Non-TTY approval channel
features.description: Give plain and JSON modes a real approval path instead of auto-denying: a configurable policy (deny-all, allow-listed tools, or external) plus an external mode that writes a pending approval request to runs/<id>/approvals/ and to the JSON stream, then waits with a configurable timeout for a decision file or a `vigil approve <runId> <requestId> --allow|--deny` invocation from another terminal or a pipeline step.
features.rationale: Plain mode currently auto-denies approvals, which silently makes the `gates` and `all` approval modes useless over SSH and in CI — the exact environments --plain exists to serve. An operator tailing a run from another terminal has no way to answer a question the cockpit would have asked.
acceptanceCriteria: An approval policy of deny-all, allow-list or external is configurable per run and defaults to the current deny-all behaviour
In external mode a pending request appears in runs/<id>/approvals/ and on the --json stream with a request id, tool name and full input
`vigil approve <runId> <requestId> --allow|--deny [--reason]` resolves a pending request from another terminal and the session proceeds accordingly
An unanswered request times out after a configurable interval and applies the configured default decision, recording the timeout as the reason
Gate approvals in `gates` mode use the same channel, and a rejection re-injects the operator's reason exactly as the TUI overlay does
All approval decisions, their source and their latency are recorded as RunEvents in events.jsonl

userStories.i_want: to answer approval prompts from a second terminal
userStories.so_that: I can use gate approvals without a TTY cockpit

userStories.i_want: an allow-list approval policy in CI
userStories.so_that: a pipeline run proceeds for safe tools and blocks on everything else instead of dying on the first prompt

features.title: Run retention, pruning and size policy
features.description: Introduce a retention policy (keep last N runs, keep runs newer than D days, cap total run-directory bytes, always keep failed runs) applied automatically at run start and exposed as `vigil prune [--dry-run]`. Add per-artifact truncation limits for oversized tool outputs, recording the original byte count and a hash of the full payload so truncation is visible and verifiable rather than silent.
features.rationale: runs/ captures full tool inputs and outputs verbatim under the plan root, is never pruned, and grows without bound. On a long-lived plan root this is both a disk problem and a compliance problem, since the same directory can contain secrets. Retention makes the run corpus a managed artifact rather than an accumulating liability.
acceptanceCriteria: Retention is configurable by run count, age and total bytes, with failed runs exempt by default
Policy is applied at run start and logged as a diagnostic naming every pruned run directory
`vigil prune --dry-run` lists exactly what would be deleted and removes nothing; without the flag it deletes and reports reclaimed bytes
Pruning never deletes the run currently in progress and never follows symlinks outside the runs root
Tool artifacts exceeding a configured byte cap are truncated with a recorded original size and a hash of the full payload, and the truncation is marked in both the artifact and the event
Default retention is documented and conservative enough that no data is lost without explicit configuration

userStories.as_a: operator with a long-lived plan root
userStories.i_want: automatic pruning of old runs
userStories.so_that: my repository does not accumulate gigabytes of agent transcripts

userStories.i_want: a bounded retention window for artifacts that may contain sensitive output
userStories.so_that: stale run data does not sit on disk indefinitely

features.title: Report coverage for mid-phase and partial runs
features.description: Generate VALIDATION reports for every run rather than only for plans that contain a phase gate or that fail. Produce a per-plan report for mid-phase runs, mark partial and interrupted runs explicitly as incomplete with the set of gates never reached, and make the ROADMAP status rewrite idempotent and non-destructive — preserving unrelated rows, writing atomically, and refusing to clobber a file that changed on disk since the run started.
features.rationale: Reports generated from observed GateRecords are the product's answer to self-graded agent validation, but they only fire for phase-gate plans, so `--only` and `--from/--to` runs produce nothing. Meanwhile the report writer rewrites ROADMAP.md in place, which is an unreviewed mutation of a user's source-controlled file.
acceptanceCriteria: Every completed plan produces a report regardless of whether it contains a phase gate
A run selected with --only or --from/--to produces a report scoped to the plans actually executed
Interrupted, budget-halted and partial runs produce a report explicitly marked incomplete, listing gates that were never reached
ROADMAP.md rewriting is idempotent: running the same report twice leaves the file byte-identical
Rows and content unrelated to the executed plans are preserved exactly, asserted by a fixture test
Report writes are atomic (write-temp-then-rename) and abort with a clear error if the target file changed on disk after the run began

userStories.as_a: operator running a single mid-phase plan
userStories.i_want: a validation report for that plan
userStories.so_that: I get evidence-backed output from partial runs, not just full phases

userStories.i_want: idempotent, non-destructive status rewriting
userStories.so_that: Vigil never produces a surprise diff in my repository

features.title: Verdict de-duplication correctness and pending-gate resolution
features.description: Replace the 30-second window heuristic for verdict de-duplication with content-and-identity-aware suppression keyed on gate id plus verdict plus reason hash, so a genuine rapid re-verdict is recorded while true duplicates from partial-stream and final-text scanning are collapsed. Resolve the empty pending-gate branch in Runner.runOne by assigning every unreached gate an explicit `not_reached` state that flows into gates.json, the reports and the run summary.
features.rationale: Two known correctness defects sit directly on the trust path: a legitimate re-verdict can be silently suppressed by a timing heuristic, and gates left pending after a failure vanish into an empty branch. An auditor reading gates.json cannot currently distinguish 'never ran' from 'not recorded', which undermines the claim that artifacts tell the whole story.
acceptanceCriteria: De-duplication is keyed on gate id, verdict and a hash of the reason rather than elapsed time
A genuine re-verdict for the same gate with a different verdict or reason is recorded as a distinct GateRecord, covered by a test that emits both within one second

features.title: Per-plan resume and resume-from-failed-gate
features.description: Replace single-id resume with full resumption state: record an SDK session id per plan in session.json alongside the gate cursor, and support `vigil run --resume <runId>` to continue a halted run from the first unsatisfied plan, plus `--resume-gate` to re-enter the failing plan's session at the failed gate with prior context rather than restarting it. features.rationale: Resume is plumbed but only one session id applies to the first plan, so a multi-phase run that fails in phase three restarts from phase one, re-spending the budget and re-running side effects. features.rationale: Re-running after a failure currently ignores everything the previous attempt produced, so stale evidence from the failed run sits in evidence/ and can satisfy an existence check on the retry — precisely the false-PASS the product exists to prevent. features.title: Strict gate identity with loud parse-time failure
features.description: Close the silent-no-op path where a gate authored without an explicit `id` can never produce a detectable verdict. GATE_RE requires a literal `VG-` prefix while the parser's fallback id is `${tag}-${n}` (e.g. validation_gate-4), which can never match. Make gate identity a validated contract: either normalise fallback ids into the matchable namespace or reject an id-less gate at parse time with a message naming the file, line and offending gate.
features.rationale: A gate that silently cannot be verified is the worst possible failure mode for a tool whose entire premise is that claims are checked. The plan looks valid, the run looks clean, and the gate is simply never enforced — a false sense of coverage in exactly the document the operator relies on. It fails silently today with no warning anywhere in the event stream.

A property test over generated gate headings (with and without ids, with unicode and punctuation) asserts parser and verdict-matcher agreement on every case

features.title: Exhaustive event spine and a genuinely pure reducer
features.description: Make the 18-variant RunEvent union exhaustive at compile time. features.rationale: The RunEvent union is the spine every other module depends on, and the UI silently drops variants it does not handle — an added event compiles clean, persists to disk, and is invisible in the cockpit. For a tool whose promise is that everything it observes is visible live, an event that reaches events.jsonl but never the operator's screen is precisely the failure the product exists to prevent. The purity violation also undermines the testability that makes the 18-case fold verifiable without a live SDK session.

features.title: Layered config resolution with provenance reporting
features.description: Replace first-file-wins config discovery, which silently drops lower-priority values and substitutes schema defaults for anything a partial file omits, with an explicit layered merge: defaults, then profile, then project config, then user config, then environment, then CLI flags. Record the provenance of every resolved key and expose it via `vigil config --explain` and in session.json.
features.rationale: A partial config file today silently discards every lower-priority value rather than merging it, so an operator who overrides one key can unknowingly reset fifteen others to defaults — including safety-relevant ones like rails and budget. With profiles landing in VG-001 and init writing files in VG-002, the number of config sources is increasing, and un-debuggable precedence becomes a support burden and a safety hazard at the same time.
acceptanceCriteria: Config resolution merges layers in documented precedence order: built-in defaults < profile < project file < user file < environment < CLI flags
A config file specifying only one key retains all other values from lower-priority layers instead of falling back to schema defaults
Rails support explicit extend and replace semantics, with the chosen semantics visible in the resolved output
`vigil config --explain` prints every resolved key with the layer and file path it came from
session.json records the resolved config plus per-key provenance so a run's configuration is auditable after the fact
Tests cover discovery order, buildEnv() precedence including unsetEnv, partial-file merging, and conflicting layer resolution

features.title: Verdict contract conformance suite and compliance telemetry
features.description: Harden the soft dependency at the heart of enforcement: the agent printing `VG-<id>: PASS|FAIL` in a parseable form. Build a fuzz and conformance corpus over realistic model output — markdown fences, bold markers, prefixes, trailing punctuation, unicode, interleaved chunk boundaries — and add runtime telemetry that raises a loud diagnostic when a plan completes with gates that never produced a verdict line.
features.rationale: Enforcement rests entirely on output formatting that Vigil does not control. A model update or a verbose formatting habit degrades enforcement silently rather than loudly: gates simply never resolve, and the run looks uneventful. An abandoned remote branch named for exactly this work shows the need was already recognised. Detecting non-compliance loudly is what keeps the trust claim honest across model changes.
acceptanceCriteria: A conformance corpus of at least 40 realistic verdict renderings is parsed correctly, covering fences, bold, leading prose, trailing punctuation and unicode
A negative corpus asserts that near-miss lines (quoted examples, the contract text itself echoed back) do not produce false verdicts
A chunk-boundary fuzz test splits each corpus entry at every byte offset and asserts LineBuffer yields identical results to the unsplit input
When a plan ends with one or more gates that never emitted a parseable verdict, Vigil emits a contract-noncompliance diagnostic naming those gates and exits non-zero
Unresolved gates appear explicitly in gates.json and in VALIDATION.md as unverified rather than being silently absent
The noncompliance rate is recorded in session.json so contract degradation across model versions is measurable over time

userStories.i_want: a loud failure when the agent stops emitting parseable verdicts
userStories.so_that: silent loss of enforcement is impossible

userStories.i_want: a conformance corpus for the verdict grammar
userStories.so_that: parser changes are provably non-regressive

features.title: Correct incremental tail follower
features.description: Fix `vigil tail`, which tracks byte offsets against a UTF-16 decoded string. Because plainLine emits ▶ ✓ ✗ and reports write ✓/✗, any non-ASCII content permanently desynchronises the follower and corrupts every subsequent line. Replace whole-file polling with positioned reads from a byte offset, decode with a streaming decoder that tolerates multi-byte characters split across reads, and self-terminate on run.end.
features.rationale: tail is the designated tool for the CI and SSH audiences this phase targets, and it is broken by the tool's own output: Vigil's plain-mode log contains the exact glyphs that desynchronise it. It also re-reads the entire file every 500ms, so cost grows quadratically with run length, and it never exits, so scripted consumers hang forever waiting for a run that finished.
acceptanceCriteria: Tail reads from a byte offset via positioned reads and never re-reads previously consumed bytes
A test writes events containing ▶ ✓ ✗ and multi-byte unicode and asserts every emitted line is byte-identical to the source line
A test splits a multi-byte character across two appends and asserts the character is emitted intact exactly once
Tail exits zero after consuming a run.end event and exits non-zero if the run ended in failure, so scripts can block on it
Following a 10,000-event file consumes O(new bytes) per poll, asserted by a read-volume benchmark rather than wall clock
--follow against a run directory that does not yet exist waits for creation rather than erroring immediately

userStories.as_a: engineer watching a run over SSH
userStories.i_want: tail output to stay readable and aligned
userStories.so_that: I can trust what I am reading mid-run

userStories.i_want: tail to exit when the run ends with a meaningful status
userStories.so_that: my pipeline step completes instead of hanging

features.title: Recursive plan discovery and tightened schemas
features.description: Remove the arbitrary two-level limit in plan discovery (phases/<dir>/<file>) in favour of bounded recursive discovery with a configurable root, depth cap and ignore patterns, and tighten permissive schemas — notably ProbeSchema, which currently accepts a probe with neither url nor command and therefore silently does nothing.
features.rationale: Plan layout is dictated by an implementation detail rather than by user need: a plan one directory deeper is simply not found, with no error explaining why. A probe with neither a url nor a command validates successfully and then never probes anything, which is the same silent-no-op class of defect as the id-less gate. Both must be resolved before pluggable plan adapters generalise discovery further.
acceptanceCriteria: Plan discovery walks recursively to a configurable maximum depth (default at least 4) honouring ignore patterns for node_modules, dist and .git
A plan nested three or more levels below the plan root is discovered and runnable
Discovery order is deterministic and documented, and a test asserts stable ordering across platforms
ProbeSchema is a discriminated union requiring exactly one of url or command; a probe with neither fails validation with a clear message
A probe with both url and command fails validation rather than silently preferring one
When discovery finds no plans, the error names the searched root, the depth limit and the ignore patterns applied

userStories.so_that: my repository layout is not dictated by a hardcoded depth

#!/bin/bash

# Auto-Build Environment Setup — vigil (006-schema-validated-sdk-message-boundary)
# Generated by Planner Agent
#
# vigil is a single TypeScript ESM CLI/TUI package. There are no servers and no
# ports to wait on: "starting the environment" means having node_modules present
# and a green typecheck/test baseline.

set -e

PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
cd "$PROJECT_ROOT"

echo "========================================"
echo "vigil — dev environment"
echo "========================================"
echo "root: $PROJECT_ROOT"

RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m'

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Toolchain check
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo -e "${RED}node not found — Node >= 20 is required${NC}"
  exit 1
fi

NODE_MAJOR="$(node -p 'process.versions.node.split(".")[0]')"
if [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -lt 20 ]; then
  echo -e "${RED}Node $NODE_MAJOR detected — package.json requires >= 20${NC}"
  exit 1
fi
echo -e "${GREEN}node $(node -v)${NC}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dependencies (this worktree ships without node_modules)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ ! -d node_modules ]; then
  echo "Installing dependencies (npm install)..."
  npm install
else
  echo -e "${GREEN}node_modules present${NC}"
fi

if [ ! -d node_modules/zod ]; then
  echo -e "${RED}zod missing after install — schemas cannot be built${NC}"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -d node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk ]; then
  echo -e "${YELLOW}warning: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk not installed — SDK typings unavailable for shape discovery${NC}"
else
  echo -e "${GREEN}claude-agent-sdk $(node -p "require('./node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/package.json').version")${NC}"
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Baseline verification
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "--- typecheck ---"
npm run typecheck

echo ""
echo "--- tests ---"
npm test

echo ""
echo "--- unsafe cast census (target: 0 in src/engine/session.ts) ---"
grep -c 'as unknown as' src/engine/session.ts || echo "0"

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo -e "${GREEN}Environment ready${NC}"
echo "========================================"
echo ""
echo "Commands:"
echo "  npm run typecheck      tsc --noEmit (strict)"
echo "  npm run build          emit dist/"
echo "  npm test               vitest run (tests/**/*.test.ts)"
echo "  npx vitest run <file>  run a single test file"
echo "  npm run dev            tsx src/cli.ts"
echo ""
echo "Record a real SDK message corpus (once the recorder lands in phase 3):"
echo "  VIGIL_RECORD_SDK=/tmp/sdk-corpus.jsonl npm run dev -- prompt 'say hi'"
echo ""

=== AUTO-BUILD PROGRESS ===

Project: vigil — Schema-validated SDK message boundary
Spec: 006-schema-validated-sdk-message-boundary

handlers onto it. New observable behaviour is added, so it is not a pure
refactor; the root cause is already known, so it is not an investigation.

- Investigated the codebase (no node_modules present; zod v4 already used in src/config.ts)

  so a new `diagnostic` kind persists with no store change
- Created project_index.json, context.json
- Created implementation_plan.json — 5 phases, 14 subtasks
- Created init.sh

Phase Summary:
- phase-0-setup          (Toolchain bootstrap):           1 subtask,  depends on []
- phase-1-foundations    (Schema module + diagnostic):    3 subtasks, depends on [phase-0-setup]
- phase-2-session-boundary (Rewire session handlers):     3 subtasks, depends on [phase-1-foundations]

Services Involved:
- vigil: single TypeScript ESM package (CLI + ink TUI). No servers, no ports, no database.

Key Design Decisions Encoded in the Plan:
1. Two-layer schemas per message type — a strict ENVELOPE (fields Vigil must have
   to act) plus an optional DETAIL layer (numerics, usage, modelUsage). An
   envelope failure skips the message with a diagnostic; a detail failure still

- Max parallel phases: 1

1	# Schema-validated SDK message boundary
 2	
 3	Replace every `as unknown as {...}` cast in the session handlers with Zod schemas that parse incoming Claude Agent SDK messages (assistant/partial/result/rate_limit/tool_use/tool_result) at the boundary. Unknown or malformed shapes are surfaced as a typed `diagnostic` RunEvent naming the offending message type and failing path, and written to disk, rather than throwing deep inside a handler or silently yielding undefined. Parsing is permissive on unknown extra fields and strict on the fields Vigil actually reads.
 4	
 5	## Rationale
 6	The tool's entire observability claim rests on correctly reading SDK messages, yet every read goes through an unchecked cast against an exactly-pinned SDK version. A schema change today produces undefined tokens, missing verdicts and silently wrong cost accounting mid-run on a production-adjacent machine. This is the highest-severity technical risk in the repository and it blocks upgrading the SDK at all.
 7	
 8	## User Stories
 9	- [object Object]
10	- [object Object]
11	
12	## Acceptance Criteria
13	- [ ] Zero `as unknown as` casts remain in src/engine/session.ts, enforced by a test that greps the source
14	- [ ] Every SDK message consumed by Vigil has a named Zod schema whose parse-failure path is unit-tested with a malformed fixture
15	- [ ] A malformed message produces a `diagnostic` RunEvent containing the message type and the failing field path, is appended to events.jsonl, and does not abort the run
16	- [ ] Unknown additional fields on an SDK message are tolerated without a diagnostic; missing required fields always produce one
17	- [ ] Cost, token and rate-limit values are read only through validated schemas; a missing total_cost_usd yields an explicit unknown rather than NaN or 0
18	- [ ] A recorded real-session message corpus parses with zero diagnostics

Key Design Decisions Encoded in the Plan:
1. Two-layer schemas per message type — a strict ENVELOPE (fields Vigil must have
   to act) plus an optional DETAIL layer (numerics, usage, modelUsage). An
   envelope failure skips the message with a diagnostic; a detail failure still
   emits a degraded event. This is what makes "diagnose but never abort"
   compatible with "missing required fields always diagnose".
2. All SDK object schemas are zod v4 LOOSE objects, so unknown extra fields are
   tolerated silently (acceptance criterion 4).
3. `session.result.costUsd` becomes `number | null`. null is the explicit unknown
   and renders as "$—" in the TUI, "unknown" in replay --plain, "$?" in `runs`.
   Never 0, never NaN (acceptance criterion 5).
4. `diagnostic` RunEvent carries messageType, schema name and issues[] with a
   formatted field path like `message.content[0].type` (acceptance criterion 3).
5. An opt-in VIGIL_RECORD_SDK=<path> recorder in session.ts is how the committed

# SDK message shapes — `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.261`

Authoritative source: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts` (the package
ships a real, complete `.d.ts` — 433 KB — so no fallback to `context.json` was needed).
Content-block and usage types resolve into `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/resources/...`
(`BetaMessage`, `BetaRawMessageStreamEvent`, `BetaUsage`, `MessageParam`).

Cross-referenced against `src/engine/session.ts` `handle()` (lines 223–298) — the only place
Vigil reads SDK messages.

Legend for **Req?**: `required` / `optional` as *declared by the SDK typings*.
`ABSENT` means the field Vigil reads **does not exist in the pinned typings at all**.

---

## 0. The message union

`SDKMessage` (sdk.d.ts:4681) is a 37-member union discriminated on `type`. Vigil's `handle()`
switch covers 7 of those `type` values; everything else falls through to the `default:` debug log.

Note that `type: 'system'` is **not** a single type — it is ~20 separate declared types each
pinned to its own `subtype` literal (`SDKSystemMessage` = `subtype:'init'`, `SDKStatusMessage` =
`subtype:'status'`, `SDKNotificationMessage`, `SDKAPIRetryMessage`, `SDKCompactBoundaryMessage`,
`SDKPermissionDeniedMessage`, `SDKSessionStateChangedMessage`, `SDKPluginInstallMessage`, …).
They share **no** common fields beyond `type` + `subtype`. This matters: a single
`SystemStatusSchema` cannot require any payload field across all four subtypes Vigil groups
together at session.ts:231.

---

## 1. `system` / `init` — `SDKSystemMessage` (sdk.d.ts:5148)

Vigil reads (session.ts:228–230, cast `as unknown as {session_id,model,tools,cwd}`):

| Field | SDK type | Req? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `'system'` | required | |
| `subtype` | `'init'` | required | |
| `session_id` | `string` | **required** | stored on `this.sessionId`; emitted as `session.init.sessionId` |
| `model` | `string` | **required** | |
| `tools` | `string[]` | **required** | Vigil already defends with `?? []`; keep `.default([])` |
| `cwd` | `string` | **required** | |

Declared but unread by Vigil: `agents?`, `apiKeySource`, `betas?`, `claude_code_version`,
`mcp_servers[]`, `permissionMode`, `slash_commands[]`, `terminal_slash_commands?`,
`output_style`, `skills[]`, `plugins[]`, `fast_mode_state?`, `fast_mode_disabled_reason?`,
`effort?`, `capabilities?`, `uuid`.

→ **`SystemInitSchema`**: `session_id` / `model` / `cwd` required strings, `tools` array of
string with `.default([])`. All four are SDK-required, so a missing one is a genuine
schema drift and must diagnose.

---

## 2. `system` / `status` \| `notification` \| `api_retry` \| `compact_boundary`

Vigil reads (session.ts:231–232): `subtype`, and `(msg as {text?: string}).text`.

⚠️ **Finding — the `text` read is only valid for one of the four subtypes.**

| Declared type | subtype | has `text`? | payload actually declared |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SDKStatusMessage` (5140) | `status` | ❌ **ABSENT** | `status: 'compacting'\|'requesting'\|null`, `permissionMode?`, `compact_result?`, `compact_error?` |
| `SDKNotificationMessage` (4811) | `notification` | ✅ `text: string` **required** | `key: string`, `text: string`, `priority`, `color?`, `timeout_ms?` |
| `SDKAPIRetryMessage` (3296) | `api_retry` | ❌ **ABSENT** | `attempt`, `max_retries`, `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status: number\|null`, `error`, `no_response?` |
| `SDKCompactBoundaryMessage` (3430) | `compact_boundary` | ❌ **ABSENT** | `compact_metadata: { trigger, pre_tokens, post_tokens?, duration_ms?, … }` |

So today Vigil logs a bare `"status"` / `"api_retry"` / `"compact_boundary"` with no detail,
and only `notification` ever produces `": <text>"`. That is existing behaviour and must be
preserved (no behaviour regression for well-formed messages).

→ **`SystemStatusSchema`**: `subtype` required string; `text` **optional** string.
Requiring `text` would diagnose on every well-formed `status`/`api_retry`/`compact_boundary`
message — a false positive. Keep it optional.

---

## 3. `stream_event` — `SDKPartialAssistantMessage` (sdk.d.ts:4826)

Vigil reads (session.ts:237–241): `event.type`, `event.delta.type`, `event.delta.text`,
`parent_tool_use_id`.

| Field | SDK type | Req? |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `'stream_event'` | required |
| `event` | `BetaRawMessageStreamEvent` | **required** |
| `parent_tool_use_id` | `string \| null` | **required** (nullable, not optional) |
| `uuid`, `session_id` | `UUID` / `string` | required (unread) |
| `ttft_ms?`, `user_message_uuid?`, `user_message_uuids?` | | optional (unread) |

`BetaRawMessageStreamEvent` = `message_start | message_delta | message_stop |
content_block_start | content_block_delta | content_block_stop`. **`type` is required on
every member; `delta` exists only on `content_block_delta` and `message_delta`.**

`BetaRawContentBlockDeltaEvent`: `{ delta: BetaRawContentBlockDelta; index: number; type: 'content_block_delta' }`.
`BetaRawContentBlockDelta` = `BetaTextDelta | BetaInputJSONDelta | BetaCitationsDelta |
BetaThinkingDelta | BetaSignatureDelta | BetaCompactionContentBlockDelta`.
`BetaTextDelta` = `{ text: string; type: 'text_delta' }` — **both required**, but only on
that one member, so `text` must be optional in our schema.

→ **`StreamEventSchema`**: `event.type` required string; `event.delta` **optional**
`{ type: string (required); text?: string }`; `parent_tool_use_id` `string|null` `.default(null)`.
Making `delta` required would diagnose on every `message_start`/`content_block_stop`.

---

## 4. `assistant` — `SDKAssistantMessage` (sdk.d.ts:3318)

Vigil reads (session.ts:246–256): `message.content[]` (`type`, `text`, `id`, `name`, `input`),
`parent_tool_use_id`.

| Field | SDK type | Req? |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `'assistant'` | required |
| `message` | `BetaMessage` | **required** |
| `message.content` | `Array<BetaContentBlock>` | **required** (array, never a string) |
| `parent_tool_use_id` | `string \| null` | **required** (nullable) |
| `error?`, `request_id?`, `aborted?`, `subagent_type?`, `timestamp?`, `context_usage?`, … | | optional (unread) |

`BetaContentBlock` is a 17-member union; every member has a required literal `type`.
Vigil handles two:

* `BetaTextBlock` = `{ citations: …|null; text: string; type: 'text' }` — `text` **required**.
* `BetaToolUseBlock` = `{ id: string; input: unknown; name: string; type: 'tool_use'; caller?; toolset_name? }`
  — `id`, `input`, `name` all **required**.

The other 15 (`thinking`, `redacted_thinking`, `server_tool_use`, `web_search_tool_result`,
`mcp_tool_use`, `compaction`, `fallback`, …) are silently skipped today and must keep being
skipped without a diagnostic.

→ **`AssistantMessageSchema`**: `message.content` = array of **loose** block objects with
`type` required string and `text` / `id` / `name` / `input` all **optional** (they are
per-member, not union-wide). `parent_tool_use_id` `string|null` `.default(null)`.
Note Vigil currently writes `m.message.content ?? []`; the SDK declares `content` required,
so a missing/non-array `content` is real drift → diagnose at path `message.content`.

---

## 5. `tool_progress` — `SDKToolProgressMessage` (sdk.d.ts:5332)

Vigil reads (session.ts:261–262): `tool_use_id`, `elapsed_time_seconds`, `heartbeat`.

| Field | SDK type | Req? |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `'tool_progress'` | required |
| `tool_use_id` | `string` | **required** |
| `tool_name` | `string` | required (unread) |
| `parent_tool_use_id` | `string \| null` | required (unread) |
| `elapsed_time_seconds` | `number` | **required** |
| `heartbeat?` | `boolean` | **optional** |
| `task_id?`, `subagent_type?`, `subagent_retry?` | | optional (unread) |
| `uuid`, `session_id` | | required (unread) |

⚠️ session.ts:262 does `m.tool_use_id.slice(-6)` — an unchecked `.slice` on a casted value.
If `tool_use_id` were ever absent this throws a `TypeError` out of `handle()` and kills the
run. This is the single most dangerous cast in the file and the clearest motivation for
`parseOrDiagnose`.

→ **`ToolProgressSchema`**: `tool_use_id` required string; `elapsed_time_seconds` number
`.default(0)`; `heartbeat` optional boolean.

---

## 6. `user` — `SDKUserMessage` (sdk.d.ts:5365)

Vigil reads (session.ts:266–274): `message.content` (string or array), and per block
`type`, `tool_use_id`, `content`, `is_error`; plus the nested `content[].text` flattening.

| Field | SDK type | Req? |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `'user'` | required |
| `message` | `MessageParam` | **required** |
| `message.content` | `string \| Array<ContentBlockParam>` | **required** (union!) |
| `parent_tool_use_id` | `string \| null` | required (unread) |
| `uuid?`, `session_id?` | | **optional** here (unlike other messages) |
| `isSynthetic?`, `tool_use_result?`, `priority?`, `shouldQuery?`, `timestamp?` | | optional (unread) |

`MessageParam` (non-beta, sdk.d.ts imports it from `@anthropic-ai/sdk/resources`) =
`{ content: string | Array<ContentBlockParam>; role: 'user'|'assistant'|'system' }`.

`ToolResultBlockParam` = `{ tool_use_id: string; type: 'tool_result'; cache_control?;
content?: string | Array<TextBlockParam|ImageBlockParam|SearchResultBlockParam|
DocumentBlockParam|ToolReferenceBlockParam|BrowserStateBlockParam>; is_error?: boolean;
toolset_name?: string|null }`.

Key points for the schema:
* `tool_use_id` is **required** on a `tool_result` block (Vigil's `&& block.tool_use_id` guard
  is defensive, not SDK-driven).
* `content` on the block is **optional** and tri-shaped: `string`, an **array of blocks**, or
  absent. Vigil's `JSON.stringify(block.content ?? "")` branch covers "absent/other".
* The nested array members carry an optional `text` — only `TextBlockParam` has
  `text: string` required; image/document members have none. So the inner `text` must be
  **optional**, which removes the `(c as {text?: string}).text` cast at session.ts:271.

→ **`UserMessageSchema`**: `message.content` = `z.union([z.string(), z.array(looseBlock)])`
where `looseBlock` = `{ type: string (required); tool_use_id?: string; content?: <string |
array of loose {type: string, text?: string} | unknown>; is_error?: boolean }`.

---

## 7. `result` — `SDKResultMessage` = `SDKResultSuccess | SDKResultError` (sdk.d.ts:5003)

Vigil reads (session.ts:281–286): `subtype`, `total_cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `num_turns`,
`usage.*`, `modelUsage`, `errors`, `result`, `is_error`.

### Fields common to **both** variants

| Field | SDK type | Req? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `'result'` | required | |
| `subtype` | `'success'` \| `'error_during_execution'` \| `'error_max_turns'` \| `'error_max_budget_usd'` \| `'error_max_structured_output_retries'` | **required** | envelope field |
| `is_error` | `boolean` | **required on both** | Vigil casts it as optional; keep optional in the schema for tolerance |
| `duration_ms` | `number` | **required** | |
| `duration_api_ms` | `number` | required (unread) | |
| `num_turns` | `number` | **required** | |
| `stop_reason` | `string \| null` | required (unread) | |
| `total_cost_usd` | `number` | **required** | ⚠️ see below |
| `usage` | `NonNullableUsage` | **required** | |
| `modelUsage` | `Record<string, ModelUsage>` | **required** | |
| `permission_denials` | `SDKPermissionDenial[]` | required (unread) | |
| `errors` | `string[]` | **required on both** | Vigil casts it optional; `m.errors?.length` is already null-safe |
| `queued_turn_count?`, `terminal_reason?`, `fast_mode_*?`, `origin?` | | optional (unread) | |
| `uuid`, `session_id` | | required (unread) | |

### Success-only

* `result: string` — **required on `SDKResultSuccess`, ABSENT on `SDKResultError`.**
  Vigil casts it as `result?: string`, which is correct behaviour: must be **optional** in
  the schema or every error result diagnoses.
* `ttft_ms?`, `ttft_stream_ms?`, `api_error_status?`, `structured_output?`,
  `deferred_tool_use?`, and a pile of timing fields — all optional (unread).

### `usage`: `NonNullableUsage` = `{ [K in keyof BetaUsage]: NonNullable<BetaUsage[K]> }`

`BetaUsage` (@anthropic-ai/sdk/resources/beta/messages/messages.d.ts):

```
cache_creation: BetaCacheCreation | null
cache_creation_input_tokens: number | null   ← Vigil reads
cache_read_input_tokens:     number | null   ← Vigil reads
fallback_credit / inference_geo / iterations / output_tokens_details
                             / server_tool_use / service_tier / speed : … | null
input_tokens:  number                        ← Vigil reads
output_tokens: number                        ← Vigil reads
```

`NonNullableUsage` strips the `| null` from every member, so on the result message all four
fields Vigil reads are **declared required numbers**. Vigil nonetheless defends with `?? 0`.

→ For `ResultDetailSchema` the four token members stay **optional numbers** mapped to `0`,
matching today's `?? 0` semantics: a degraded result must still emit, not vanish.

### `modelUsage`: `Record<string, ModelUsage>`

`ModelUsage` = `{ inputTokens, outputTokens, thinkingTokens?, cacheReadInputTokens,
cacheCreationInputTokens, webSearchRequests, costUSD, contextWindow, maxOutputTokens,
canonicalModel?, provider?, costBasis? }`. Vigil only reads `costUSD`, `inputTokens`,
`outputTokens` (and only stores the record wholesale onto `session.result.modelUsage`).

### ⚠️ `total_cost_usd` — the cost criterion

The SDK declares it **required `number` on both variants**, but the doc comment is explicit:

> "Crash/startup-error results may carry zeroed values … An estimate, not a billing statement."

A *zeroed* cost and an *absent* cost are different facts, and the current
`m.total_cost_usd ?? 0` collapses them. That is exactly acceptance criterion 5: absent →
explicit `null` + a diagnostic at path `total_cost_usd`; present → the number verbatim
(including a legitimate `0`).

→ **`ResultEnvelopeSchema`**: `subtype` required string, `is_error` optional boolean.
→ **`ResultDetailSchema`**: `total_cost_usd` / `duration_ms` / `num_turns` **optional**
numbers; `usage` optional loose object of optional numbers; `modelUsage` optional record;
`errors` optional `string[]`; `result` optional string. Splitting the two is what lets a
detail failure still emit a degraded `session.result`.

---

## 8. `rate_limit_event` — `SDKRateLimitEvent` (sdk.d.ts:4923)

Vigil reads (session.ts:290–292): `rate_limit_info.status`, `.rateLimitType`,
`.unifiedWindows[k].utilization`.

| Field | SDK type | Req? |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `'rate_limit_event'` | required |
| `rate_limit_info` | `SDKRateLimitInfo` | **required** |
| `uuid`, `session_id` | | required (unread) |

`SDKRateLimitInfo` (sdk.d.ts:4938) — **complete declared field list**:

| Field | SDK type | Req? |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `'allowed' \| 'allowed_warning' \| 'rejected'` | **required** |
| `resetsAt?` | `number` | optional |
| `rateLimitType?` | `'five_hour' \| 'seven_day' \| 'seven_day_opus' \| 'seven_day_sonnet' \| 'seven_day_overage_included' \| 'overage'` | optional |
| `utilization?` | `number` | **optional — top level, not nested** |
| `overageStatus?`, `overageResetsAt?`, `overageDisabledReason?`, `isUsingOverage?`, `overageInUse?`, `surpassedThreshold?`, `errorCode?`, `canUserPurchaseCredits?`, `hasChargeableSavedPaymentMethod?` | | optional |

### ⚠️⚠️ Finding — `unifiedWindows` DOES NOT EXIST in 0.3.261

```
$ grep -c unifiedWindows node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts   → 0
$ grep -rl unifiedWindows node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/          → (no files)
```

Zero hits in `sdk.d.ts`, `sdk.mjs`, `bridge.d.ts`/`bridge.mjs`, `browser-sdk.*` — neither in
the typings nor in the shipped runtime bundle. `info?.unifiedWindows` at session.ts:291 is
**permanently `undefined`**, so `util` is always `""` and Vigil has never once rendered a
rate-limit utilisation figure. This is precisely the class of silent, undetectable breakage
the spec was written to eliminate, and it is already live in `main`.

The real per-request utilisation lives at `rate_limit_info.utilization` (a single top-level
`number`, `0`–`1`), alongside `rateLimitType` which names the window.

→ **`RateLimitEventSchema`**: `rate_limit_info.status` **required** string (SDK-required —
a missing `status` is genuine drift and must diagnose); `rateLimitType`, `utilization`,
`resetsAt` optional; `unifiedWindows` kept as an **optional** loose record of
`{ utilization?: number }` so the existing (dead) code path keeps compiling and would light
up if a future SDK reintroduces the field. Because it is optional, its absence in 0.3.261
produces **no diagnostic** — the corpus in subtask-3-4 must therefore parse clean with only
`status` present.

**Scope note:** fixing the empty utilisation string by reading the top-level `utilization` is
a behaviour change beyond this spec's stated criteria. Phase 2 (subtask-2-3) should preserve
today's output exactly; the finding is recorded here so it can be raised separately.

---

## 9. Summary — schema field table for subtask-1-1

| Export | Required fields (diagnose if missing) | Optional / defaulted |
|---|---|---|
| `SdkEnvelopeSchema` | `type: string` | — |
| `SystemInitSchema` | `session_id`, `model`, `cwd` | `tools: string[] = []` |
| `SystemStatusSchema` | `subtype: string` | `text?: string` |
| `StreamEventSchema` | `event.type: string` | `event.delta?: {type: string; text?: string}`, `parent_tool_use_id = null` |
| `AssistantMessageSchema` | `message.content: Array<{type: string, …}>` | block `text?`/`id?`/`name?`/`input?`, `parent_tool_use_id = null` |
| `ToolProgressSchema` | `tool_use_id: string` | `elapsed_time_seconds = 0`, `heartbeat?` |
| `UserMessageSchema` | `message.content: string \| Array<{type: string, …}>` | block `tool_use_id?`/`content?`/`is_error?` |
| `ResultEnvelopeSchema` | `subtype: string` | `is_error?: boolean` |
| `ResultDetailSchema` | — (all optional by design) | `total_cost_usd?`, `duration_ms?`, `num_turns?`, `usage?`, `modelUsage?`, `errors?`, `result?` |
| `RateLimitEventSchema` | `rate_limit_info.status: string` | `rateLimitType?`, `utilization?`, `resetsAt?`, `unifiedWindows?` |

Every object schema must be `z.looseObject(...)` (zod v4) so the large tails of unread
optional fields documented above — and any field a future SDK adds — pass through silently.

---

## 10. Findings that affect later subtasks

1. **`unifiedWindows` does not exist** (§8). Must be optional; the corpus must not include it
   as a required-to-pass field. Existing behaviour (empty utilisation string) is preserved.
2. **`text` exists only on `subtype:'notification'`** (§2). `SystemStatusSchema.text` must be
   optional or three of the four grouped subtypes false-positive on every message.
3. **`result` (the text) is success-only** (§7). Must be optional or every error result
   diagnoses.
4. **`event.delta` is per-stream-event-member** (§3). Must be optional or every
   `message_start` / `content_block_stop` diagnoses.
5. **`tool_use_id.slice(-6)` at session.ts:262 can throw** (§5) — the concrete "aborts the
   run" hazard `parseOrDiagnose` removes.
6. **`total_cost_usd` is SDK-required but documented as zeroable on crash results** (§7) —
   absent ⇒ `null` + diagnostic; present ⇒ verbatim, including a real `0`.
7. **`assistant.message.content` is SDK-required**, so Vigil's `?? []` masks real drift (§4)
   — the schema should diagnose at `message.content`.
8. Blocks Vigil ignores (`thinking`, `server_tool_use`, 13 others) must keep being ignored
   **without** a diagnostic — only a block missing its required `type` diagnoses.

221	| `errors` | `string[]` | **required on both** | Vigil casts it optional; `m.errors?.length` is already null-safe |
222	| `queued_turn_count?`, `terminal_reason?`, `fast_mode_*?`, `origin?` | | optional (unread) | |
223	| `uuid`, `session_id` | | required (unread) | |
224	
225	### Success-only
226	
227	* `result: string` — **required on `SDKResultSuccess`, ABSENT on `SDKResultError`.**
228	  Vigil casts it as `result?: string`, which is correct behaviour: must be **optional** in
229	  the schema or every error result diagnoses.
230	* `ttft_ms?`, `ttft_stream_ms?`, `api_error_status?`, `structured_output?`,
231	  `deferred_tool_use?`, and a pile of timing fields — all optional (unread).
232	
233	### `usage`: `NonNullableUsage` = `{ [K in keyof BetaUsage]: NonNullable<BetaUsage[K]> }`
234	
235	`BetaUsage` (@anthropic-ai/sdk/resources/beta/messages/messages.d.ts):
236	
237	```
238	cache_creation: BetaCacheCreation | null
239	cache_creation_input_tokens: number | null   ← Vigil reads
240	cache_read_input_tokens:     number | null   ← Vigil reads
241	fallback_credit / inference_geo / iterations / output_tokens_details
242	                             / server_tool_use / service_tier / speed : … | null
243	input_tokens:  number                        ← Vigil reads
244	output_tokens: number                        ← Vigil reads
245	```
246	
247	`NonNullableUsage` strips the `| null` from every member, so on the result message all four
248	fields Vigil reads are **declared required numbers**. Vigil nonetheless defends with `?? 0`.
249	
250	→ For `ResultDetailSchema` the four token members stay **optional numbers** mapped to `0`,
251	matching today's `?? 0` semantics: a degraded result must still emit, not vanish.
252	
253	### `modelUsage`: `Record<string, ModelUsage>`
254	
255	`ModelUsage` = `{ inputTokens, outputTokens, thinkingTokens?, cacheReadInputTokens,
256	cacheCreationInputTokens, webSearchRequests, costUSD, contextWindow, maxOutputTokens,
257	canonicalModel?, provider?, costBasis? }`. Vigil only reads `costUSD`, `inputTokens`,
258	`outputTokens` (and only stores the record wholesale onto `session.result.modelUsage`).
259	
260	### ⚠️ `total_cost_usd` — the cost criterion
261	
262	The SDK declares it **required `number` on both variants**, but the doc comment is explicit:
263	
264	> "Crash/startup-error results may carry zeroed values … An estimate, not a billing statement."
265	
266	A *zeroed* cost and an *absent* cost are different facts, and the current
267	`m.total_cost_usd ?? 0` collapses them. That is exactly acceptance criterion 5: absent →
268	explicit `null` + a diagnostic at path `total_cost_usd`; present → the number verbatim
269	(including a legitimate `0`).
270	
271	→ **`ResultEnvelopeSchema`**: `subtype` required string, `is_error` optional boolean.
272	→ **`ResultDetailSchema`**: `total_cost_usd` / `duration_ms` / `num_turns` **optional**
273	numbers; `usage` optional loose object of optional numbers; `modelUsage` optional record;
274	`errors` optional `string[]`; `result` optional string. Splitting the two is what lets a
275	detail failure still emit a degraded `session.result`.
276	
277	---
278	
279	## 8. `rate_limit_event` — `SDKRateLimitEvent` (sdk.d.ts:4924)
280	
281	Vigil reads (session.ts:290–292): `rate_limit_info.status`, `.rateLimitType`,
282	`.unifiedWindows[k].utilization`.
283	
284	| Field | SDK type | Req? |
285	|---|---|---|
286	| `type` | `'rate_limit_event'` | required |
287	| `rate_limit_info` | `SDKRateLimitInfo` | **required** |
288	| `uuid`, `session_id` | | required (unread) |
289	
290	`SDKRateLimitInfo` (sdk.d.ts:4937) — **complete declared field list**:
291	
292	| Field | SDK type | Req? |
293	|---|---|---|
294	| `status` | `'allowed' \| 'allowed_warning' \| 'rejected'` | **required** |
295	| `resetsAt?` | `number` | optional |
296	| `rateLimitType?` | `'five_hour' \| 'seven_day' \| 'seven_day_opus' \| 'seven_day_sonnet' \| 'seven_day_overage_included' \| 'overage'` | optional |
297	| `utilization?` | `number` | **optional — top level, not nested** |
298	| `overageStatus?`, `overageResetsAt?`, `overageDisabledReason?`, `isUsingOverage?`, `overageInUse?`, `surpassedThreshold?`, `errorCode?`, `canUserPurchaseCredits?`, `hasChargeableSavedPaymentMethod?` | | optional |
299	
300	### ⚠️⚠️ Finding — `unifiedWindows` DOES NOT EXIST in 0.3.261
301	
302	```
303	$ grep -c unifiedWindows node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts   → 0
304	$ grep -rl unifiedWindows node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/          → (no files)
305	```
306	
307	Zero hits in `sdk.d.ts`, `sdk.mjs`, `bridge.d.ts`/`bridge.mjs`, `browser-sdk.*` — neither in
308	the typings nor in the shipped runtime bundle. `info?.unifiedWindows` at session.ts:291 is
309	**permanently `undefined`**, so `util` is always `""` and Vigil has never once rendered a
310	rate-limit utilisation figure. This is precisely the class of silent, undetectable breakage
311	the spec was written to eliminate, and it is already live in `main`.
312	
313	The real per-request utilisation lives at `rate_limit_info.utilization` (a single top-level
314	`number`, `0`–`1`), alongside `rateLimitType` which names the window.
315	
316	→ **`RateLimitEventSchema`**: `rate_limit_info.status` **required** string (SDK-required —
317	a missing `status` is genuine drift and must diagnose); `rateLimitType`, `utilization`,
318	`resetsAt` optional; `unifiedWindows` kept as an **optional** loose record of
319	`{ utilization?: number }` so the existing (dead) code path keeps compiling and would light
320	up if a future SDK reintroduces the field. Because it is optional, its absence in 0.3.261
321	produces **no diagnostic** — the corpus in subtask-3-4 must therefore parse clean with only
322	`status` present.
323	
324	**Scope note:** fixing the empty utilisation string by reading the top-level `utilization` is
325	a behaviour change beyond this spec's stated criteria. Phase 2 (subtask-2-3) should preserve
326	today's output exactly; the finding is recorded here so it can be raised separately.
327	
328	---
329	
330	## 9. Summary — schema field table for subtask-1-1
331	
332	| Export | Required fields (diagnose if missing) | Optional / defaulted |
333	|---|---|---|
334	| `SdkEnvelopeSchema` | `type: string` | — |
335	| `SystemInitSchema` | `session_id`, `model`, `cwd` | `tools: string[] = []` |
336	| `SystemStatusSchema` | `subtype: string` | `text?: string` |
337	| `StreamEventSchema` | `event.type: string` | `event.delta?: {type: string; text?: string}`, `parent_tool_use_id = null` |
338	| `AssistantMessageSchema` | `message.content: Array<{type: string, …}>` | block `text?`/`id?`/`name?`/`input?`, `parent_tool_use_id = null` |
339	| `ToolProgressSchema` | `tool_use_id: string` | `elapsed_time_seconds = 0`, `heartbeat?` |
340	| `UserMessageSchema` | `message.content: string \| Array<{type: string, …}>` | block `tool_use_id?`/`content?`/`is_error?` |
341	| `ResultEnvelopeSchema` | `subtype: string` | `is_error?: boolean` |
342	| `ResultDetailSchema` | — (all optional by design) | `total_cost_usd?`, `duration_ms?`, `num_turns?`, `usage?`, `modelUsage?`, `errors?`, `result?` |
343	| `RateLimitEventSchema` | `rate_limit_info.status: string` | `rateLimitType?`, `utilization?`, `resetsAt?`, `unifiedWindows?` |
344	
345	Every object schema must be `z.looseObject(...)` (zod v4) so the large tails of unread
346	optional fields documented above — and any field a future SDK adds — pass through silently.
347	
348	---
349	
350	## 10. Findings that affect later subtasks
351	
352	1. **`unifiedWindows` does not exist** (§8). Must be optional; the corpus must not include it
353	   as a required-to-pass field. Existing behaviour (empty utilisation string) is preserved.
354	2. **`text` exists only on `subtype:'notification'`** (§2). `SystemStatusSchema.text` must be
355	   optional or three of the four grouped subtypes false-positive on every message.
356	3. **`result` (the text) is success-only** (§7). Must be optional or every error result
357	   diagnoses.
358	4. **`event.delta` is per-stream-event-member** (§3). Must be optional or every
359	   `message_start` / `content_block_stop` diagnoses.
360	5. **`tool_use_id.slice(-6)` at session.ts:262 can throw** (§5) — the concrete "aborts the
361	   run" hazard `parseOrDiagnose` removes.
362	6. **`total_cost_usd` is SDK-required but documented as zeroable on crash results** (§7) —

364	7. **`assistant.message.content` is SDK-required**, so Vigil's `?? []` masks real drift (§4)

367	   **without** a diagnostic — only a block missing its required `type` diagnoses.

# Gotchas and Pitfalls

Things to watch out for in this codebase:

- SDK 0.3.261 has NO `unifiedWindows` field anywhere (0 hits in sdk.d.ts, sdk.mjs, bridge.*, browser-sdk.*). session.ts:291 reads it, so rate-limit utilisation has ALWAYS rendered as an empty string. Keep it optional in the schema or the subtask-3-4 corpus can never parse clean.
- `text` on a system message exists ONLY on subtype 'notification'. status/api_retry/compact_boundary have no `text` - SystemStatusSchema.text MUST be optional or 3 of 4 subtypes false-positive every message.
- SDKResultSuccess has `result: string` but SDKResultError does NOT - `result` must be optional or every error result diagnoses.
- `event.delta` only exists on content_block_delta/message_delta members of BetaRawMessageStreamEvent - must be optional or message_start/content_block_stop diagnose.
- type:'system' is ~20 separate declared types each pinned to its own subtype literal, sharing NO fields beyond type+subtype.
- session.ts:262 calls m.tool_use_id.slice(-6) on a casted value - a missing tool_use_id throws a TypeError out of handle() and kills the run. The concrete run-abort hazard.
- assistant message.content is SDK-REQUIRED, so Vigil's `?? []` masks real drift; the schema should diagnose at path message.content.
- The 15 BetaContentBlock members Vigil ignores (thinking, server_tool_use, mcp_tool_use...) must keep being skipped WITHOUT a diagnostic - only a block missing its required `type` diagnoses.
- total_cost_usd is declared required on both result variants but documented as zeroed on crash results - absent => null + diagnostic, present => verbatim including a real 0.
- Subtask deliverables that live under .auto-claude/ produce NO git commit (the pathspec ':!.auto-claude' excludes them). That is correct, not a failure.
- zod v4 issue.path is PropertyKey[]; array indices arrive as numbers, so formatPath must render them as [n] to produce message.content[0].type
- z.array(BlockSchema) fails the WHOLE message when one element is bad - a per-block schema plus a content:array-of-unknown envelope schema is needed when sibling elements must still be processed
- z.looseObject does not deep-clone unknown values, so safeParse on a circular object succeeds rather than hanging - but parseWith still wraps safeParse in try/catch as a guarantee
- JSON.stringify(undefined) returns undefined (not a string), so sampleOf needs the ?? String(input) fallback
- npm run build writes dist/ (gitignored) - never stage it
# Code Patterns

Established patterns to follow in this codebase:

- zod v4 (4.5.4) is installed - z.looseObject() is available and is the required idiom for SDK message schemas; never z.strictObject.
- NodeNext ESM: every relative import must end in .js even from .ts sources.
- RunStore.append() JSON-stringifies EVERY event to events.jsonl before its per-kind switch, so a new RunEvent kind needs no store.ts change.
- Adding a RunEvent variant requires updating exactly two switches: src/state/reducer.ts reduce() and src/cli.ts plainLine().
- zod is v4.5.4: z.looseObject() exists and is the right passthrough primitive; z.record() needs an explicit key schema (z.record(z.string(), X))
- Schemas live as module-level consts with a z.infer type alias directly beneath, mirroring src/config.ts
- tsconfig is strict + NodeNext, so intra-src imports must carry the .js extension
